transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maria Lopez (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Samir Patel (CTO - Aurora Clinic), Janelle Ortiz (Platform Eng), Marcus Reed (Security), Lina Gomez (Product)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting and multi-tenant controls. Customer cares about per-clinic quotas, per-project billing, predictable throttling (not full outage), and auditability for compliance. Demonstrated Console configs and API behaviors.

[00:00] Maria Lopez (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro i'm maria redwood ae, with ethan and priya from our se team. samir, janelle, marcus, thanks for taking the time. we planned a focused demo on org/project keys, rate limits and quotas. we want to show both console + api behavior and answer security questions.

[00:25] Dr. Samir Patel (Aurora): thanks maria. main thing for us is multi-tenant control; we run clinic tenants across states and need per-tenant quotas, plus audit logs for compliance. also curious about burst behavior and what happens when a tenant exceeds rate.

[00:45] Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE): great, yeah we'll show two pieces: console side for ops, then live API calls to illustrate enforcement. quick note, some of the field names in the console are internal shorthand, sorry if the generated transcript autocorrects, you'll see orgs/projects as Org > Project in the UI.

[01:10] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): jumping in, here's why this matters: org-level controls give you global caps and admin RBAC; project keys are for per-application tenant isolation and billing separation. you can attach quota policies to projects or to keys directly.

[01:45] Janelle Ortiz (Aurora): can you do different token quotas per project? like clinic-a gets higher tokens/day than clinic-b?

[01:52] Ethan: yes, you can set quotas at project granularity, tokens/day, rps, concurrency, and burst windows. we showed an example earlier where project A had 5M tokens/day and project B 1M tokens/day. the console enforces it and the api returns 429 with details.

[02:15] Marcus Reed (Aurora): on 429s, do you expose headers for remaining quota? we need visibility for our retry logic and alerting.

[02:22] Priya: yep, we expose x-rdinference-limit and x-rdinference-remaining headers (note: header names in transcript may differ slightly) plus a structured json body with code and reason. we also stream events to audit logs and you can push those to your S3/logging endpoint.

[02:50] Lina Gomez (Aurora): and billing, if we have project-level keys, is usage billed per project? we'd like to attribute costs to teams.

[02:58] Maria: yes projects map to billing tags; you can export per-project metrics to our billing CSV or to your internal cost system. Projects can have separate rate limit policies and quotas, and those metrics show up in the Console's cost table.

[03:20] Ethan: demo time, i'm going to share screen, console -> org settings -> projects. bear with me, there's sometimes a slight layout change across regions.

[04:05] [screen share noises] Ethan: here we have our org "Aurora-POC" and three projects listed: intake-api, mobile-chat, analytics. i'll click into intake-api. you can see quota policy: 2M tokens/day, 500 rps burst window 10s, concurrency soft limit 50.

[04:35] Janelle: can those limits be overridden per key? like we have partner integrations that should have separate throttles.

[04:42] Ethan: yes keys inherit project defaults but you can create a key-level override. for partner keys we usually create a 'partner' project or create a key-level policy that puts a hard cap at say 100k tokens/day.

[05:05] Priya: a couple of enforcement behaviors to note: we support soft quota (throttling with warnings) and hard quota (rejections). soft quota will route to a fallback model or queue requests depending on policy; hard quota returns 429 immediately.

[05:30] Marcus: fallback model as in lower-cost, lower-latency model? i'm concerned about data residency if we route.

[05:40] Ethan: right, fallback can be to a smaller open model variant in the same region with the same data controls. for private deployments or VPC, fallback respects the same network boundaries, we don't route outside your VPC unless configured.

[06:05] Dr. Samir: what's the granularity of audit logs? we need user-level and key-level events for 90-day retention for audits.

[06:14] Priya: audit logs include key_id, project_id, route, tokens_consumed, timestamp, and response codes. retention and export are configurable, out of the box we store 30/90/365 day options depending on plan, and you can push to your S3 or SIEM for long-term.

[06:40] [08:00] Ethan: now i'll show an API example; we'll send a burst of requests using the project key. you should see the remaining header drop and then the 429 with the reason.

[08:15] [terminal clacking] Ethan: hitting /v1/generate with api key, first two succeed, you can see headers: x-rdinference-remaining: 1498, x-rdinference-limit: 1500. after we exceed, response: {"error":{"code":"quota_exceeded","message":"project token quota exceeded"}} and status 429.

[09:10] Janelle: can we customize the error message or codes? our app expects a specific shape for retries.

[09:18] Ethan: you can map errors at the API gateway layer in Dedicated/private installs, but for hosted we provide the standard error shape. we can add a middleware in your edge layer to remap if needed.

[09:40] Maria: quick question, timeline and decision drivers? are you leaning hosted or private/dedicated for the pilot?

[09:50] Dr. Samir: for the pilot we prefer hosted to move faster, but we need to validate SSO and encryption. production might require dedicated or private for data residency.

[10:05] Marcus: on encryption, do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?

[10:12] Priya: yes we offer KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure) for hosted enterprise customers; keys can be customer-managed for stored artifacts and logs. for in-flight TLS we use standard TLS, and you can bring private endpoints in dedicated.

[10:40] Lina: how do we handle global quotas across regions? we have clinics in EU and US; we'd like local quotas plus a global aggregate cap.

[10:50] Ethan: we support hierarchical policies, org-wide global cap plus region-specific project policies. enforcement can be local (per-region) with a replicated counter, or global which aggregates across regions with eventual consistency; we recommend local caps for strict compliance and global aggregate for cost control.

[11:25] [12:00] Ethan: back to console, i'll show the policy editor, you can set windows, sliding windows, strict rps, and token budgets. there's a preview simulation that estimates expected rejections at different traffic profiles.

[12:40] Janelle: that simulation, is it based on historical traffic or synthetic?

[12:45] Ethan: it uses your historical metrics if available, otherwise synthetic profile. for pilots we can seed it with your last 7 days of traffic to calibrate.

[13:05] Marcus: curious about rate-limit headers for webhooks or async jobs; we use async processors with long tails. does Redwood support queueing backpressure?

[13:14] Priya: yes for async flows we recommend our batched async endpoints with queue semantics; you can set concurrency and max in-flight jobs per project. backpressure is surfaced via status codes and webhook callbacks.

[13:40] Dr. Samir: about keys, how do you rotate keys without downtime? we need zero-downtime rotation for long-lived integrations.

[13:50] Ethan: key rotation is seamless: you can create a new key, attach same policies, and perform phased rollout. the Console shows active keys and usage; you can rotate and set deprecated flags with a grace period.

[14:15] [14:30] Janelle: are there limits on number of keys per project? we have many partner connectors.

[14:35] Maria: default soft limit is 500 keys/project, we can increase for enterprise. we also support key groups for easier policy assignment.

[14:50] Marcus: compliance question, do you provide SOC2 report and penetration test results?

[14:56] Priya: yes we provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs to customers under NDA. i'll share the security pack after the call. we also have a SOC link in the security center.

[15:10] Ethan: next i'm going to demo a failure mode, how we gracefully degrade when a project hits soft quota. i'll flip a policy to soft and trigger a fallback.

[15:25] [terminal clack] Ethan: sending requests, first responses are to the primary model, then when threshold hit, responses come back from a smaller model. logs show fallback: true, fallback_model: redwood-small-v1. you can configure policy to route to cached completions as well.

[16:00] Lina: important, if we do fallback to smaller models, is there any change in data handling? we need same retention and no external routing.

[16:08] Priya: correct, same data retention and processing rules apply; fallback occurs within your configured region and deployment mode. we do not send data outside your org's permitted boundaries.

[16:35] Dr. Samir: what about simultaneous quota enforcement and billing attribution? if fallback uses small model we still bill tokens separately?

[16:45] Ethan: billing is token-based per model; fallback tokens are billed at the fallback model's rate. the Console shows per-model cost breakdown with attribution by project/key. we can also apply cost caps to projects to avoid surprise bills.

[17:10] Janelle: can we set alerts when a project reaches 75% of quota?

[17:15] Maria: yes alerting is built-in, email, webhook, and PagerDuty integrations. thresholds configurable at 50/75/90/100%.

[17:35] Marcus: for the pilot we want to run a two-week benchmark with 95th percentile latency SLAs. can you support generating load from your side or do we need to orchestrate?

[17:45] Ethan: we can help design benchmark tests and provide a harness; typically customers run load from their env to mimic network and auth setups. we can run parallel load from our test infra if you want a controlled baseline.

[18:10] Dr. Samir: what metrics will you need from our side?

[18:15] Priya: tokens/day, peak rps, % of traffic that needs streaming, average and p95 seq length, expected concurrency. Janelle said she'll share current qps and token estimates after this call.

[18:40] [20:00] Maria: quick pause, any red flags yet?

[20:05] Lina: main concerns are key rotation, audit log retention, and how fallback affects billing. otherwise looks promising.

[20:20] Marcus: also SSO, can we use our Okta for SAML?

[20:25] Priya: yes Okta/SAML and SCIM provisioning for user management and RBAC. we'll share the exact metadata endpoints.

[20:40] Ethan: one more advanced feature, dynamic token buckets per project using ML-driven smoothing; it allows flexible burst without impacting latency. it's off by default and used for spike-prone workloads.

[21:05] Janelle: interesting. is that safe for regulated workloads?

[21:12] Ethan: yes it's compatible with compliance; policies are auditable and you can disable it for a project.

[21:40] [23:00] Maria: ok recap, maria: we'll send pricing + pilot + security pack; ethan will share SOC2, network diagrams, and a demo recording. janelle to share traffic estimates. after we get those we'll schedule a 2-week pilot kickoff.

[23:20] Dr. Samir: sounds good. can you include a sample policy json we can drop into our IaC?

[23:28] Ethan: yes i'll attach policy templates, project policy, key override, and org-level cap.

[23:45] [24:00] Maria: any final questions?

[24:05] Lina: just one, can we do per-user quotas inside a project? for example limit a single partner user to 10k tokens/day.

[24:12] Priya: you can scope policies to client_id (user) or api_key; we usually recommend api_key for clear boundaries but client-level quotas are supported via our policy engine.

[24:40] [25:00] Marcus: ok thanks everyone. we'll look for the docs and security pack.

[25:10] Ethan: i'll share the recording and the policy templates.

[25:25] Maria: thanks all, we'll follow up with next steps and schedule the pilot kickoff. have a great afternoon.

End of call.

Notes: transcription contains occasional recognition errors (header names, exact UI labels). References to header names (x-rdinference-*) are examples, actual prod headers may be different.
